NextDoor.Company started as a weekend hackathon project because I kept seeing growth news about startups and their hiring spree, but at the same time my friends kept complaining: "If startups are hiring actively, where are they?" or "I can't find good startups on LinkedIn or Indeed anymore."  
  
So I built a map-first job discovery platform that shows you top-tier startups actively hiring near you. Since August last year, I've been hand curating top-tier startups globally, and now it hosts 16,000+ live job openings, updated every week. [...] Framer AI Agents

Hello Product Hunt 👋🏼  
  
As someone who spends a lot of time around founders, one thing I've noticed is how broken startup hiring discovery still is.  
  
Great startups are hiring every day, yet finding them often means jumping between LinkedIn, company websites, X and funding databases.  
  
Instead of being another job board, NextDoor.Company helps you discover high-quality startups on a map and gives you the context that actually matters.  
  
Have seen how obsessed Sankalp is in solving for this space and I'll let him tell the story behind why he built it.

results.content:
A map and radius-first interface is the main draw: users can zoom from very close range to city-scale exploration and check what’s happening anywhere, even before arriving. That makes it especially useful for newcomers, planners, and anyone who wants lightweight “what’s happening here” discovery without the heavier social dynamics that can come with traditional neighborhood forums.

For local businesses and organizers, the handbill model can be a better fit than general neighborhood posting because it matches how local promos and micro-events behave in real life. The main trade-off versus Nextdoor is that it’s less about ongoing neighbor relationships and more about situational, place-based discovery.

### Best for [...] ### Standout features
